svg.title: How close are we to replacing Python’s re?
svg.desc: Python 3.14.6 has 165 original regular-expression test methods: 152 are public compatibility tests and 13 are explicitly waived CPython-private tests from two named classes. Both Python baseline runs pass 151 public methods and skip one genuine debug-build method. Rust processed the same 152 records: 139 pass, 11 expose test-harness interference, one exposes a real missing _compile pickling hook, and the same debug-only test is skipped. C and Zig have not run the original public tests. Current speed and memory remain unmeasured.
svg.text: How close are we to replacing Python’s re?
Three independently built engines · compared with Python 3.14.6
original Python test methods
public compatibility records
waived CPython-private tests
qualified replacement engines
What is included in the Python baseline?
165 original methods = 152 public compatibility records + 13 private tests from 2 named classes.
Public baseline: 151 passing methods + 1 genuine debug-build-only skip. No public test is waived.
DebugTests: 4 tests of CPython’s private matching-opcode display.
ImplementationTest: 9 private compiler, _sre, type-internal and deprecated implementation tests.
Original correctness checks
The same 223,198 initial cases for each engine · 49 categories

What happened in the full public Python test?
Rust accounted for all 152 public test records and both sets of 304 engine guards.
Rust
NOT YET COMPATIBLE
genuinely passing methods
test-harness errors
real missing _compile
debug-only skip
139 passes + 11 harness errors + 1 real candidate error + 1 debug-only skip = 152
Why the failures are different
11 errors come from the test harness blocking Python’s own warning and assertion helpers.
They are not 11 demonstrated regex-engine mismatches.
1 real drop-in gap: Python’s pickling test cannot import Rust’s required _compile helper.
This genuine original-test incompatibility still needs a fix.
C
NOT RUN
No result claimed for the 152 public Python records.
Zig
NOT RUN
No result claimed for the 152 public Python records.
All earlier test-setup failures remain preserved
Missing bridge wiring · anti-delegation import guard · candidate-free correctness-controller guard
All three stopped before the first test; none is counted as a matching-engine mismatch.
Overall: no from-scratch engine has yet passed every required public Python test.
Current speed and memory: NOT MEASURED · final holdout: NOT ACCESSED.
